#1
L: This, but, to-you, the-most-secret, I-shall-declare, to-one-free-of-malice: knowledge combined-with-realization, which having-known you-shall-be-released from-evil.
I: To you, who bear me no ill will, I shall declare this most secret thing: knowledge joined with direct realization, knowing which you shall be freed from evil.
N: This opens the chapter's title-teaching (rāja-vidyā, rāja-guhyam, named at verse 2) with a direct address: anasūyave, 'to one free of malice/envy, uncensorious', names Arjuna as a fit recipient because he does not carp or cavil at what he is told. Vijñāna-sahitam, 'combined with vijñāna [realization, experiential knowledge]', distinguishes the jñāna about to be taught from mere theoretical knowledge. Sandhi: यज्ज्ञात्वा packs yat + jñātvā (-t + j- → -j jñ-, assimilation); मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् is mokṣyase + aśubhāt (avagraha).
#2
L: Royal-knowledge, royal-secret, pure, this, supreme, directly-comprehensible, dharma-conforming, very-easy to-do, imperishable.
I: It is royal knowledge, the royal secret, pure and supreme, verifiable by direct experience, in keeping with dharma, very easy to practice, and imperishable.
N: A cascade of nominal epithets, all describing the jñāna announced in verse 1 (rāja-vidyā is feminine, agreeing with vidyā's own inherent gender, while the rest are neuter, agreeing with jñānam — a normal mismatch when nouns and adjectives are simply juxtaposed in apposition rather than made to agree). Pratyakṣa-avagamam, 'directly comprehensible', claims this knowledge is verified by one's own experience, not only by scriptural authority. Sandhi: प्रत्यक्षावगमं is pratyakṣa + avagamam (a+a→ā); पवित्रमिदमुत्तमम् and कर्तुमव्ययम् both show a final -m simply written joined before a following vowel, with no phonetic change (pavitram+idam+uttamam, kartum+avyayam).
#3
L: Faithless men, of-this dharma, O scorcher-of-the-foe, not-attaining me, return on-the-path of-death-and-transmigration.
I: Men who lack faith in this dharma, Parantapa, fail to reach me and return instead to the path of death and rebirth.
N: A warning that closes the opening address: those without śraddhā, 'faith', in this dharma cannot attain Kṛṣṇa and remain on the path of mṛtyu-saṃsāra, 'death and transmigration'. Parantapa, 'scorcher of the foe', an epithet of Arjuna. Sandhi: पुरुषा is puruṣāḥ with its visarga simply dropped (not changed to -o) before the voiced dh- of dharmasya, because the stem vowel is ā (long), not a (short) — a distinction that recurs often in this chapter: -aḥ (short a) before a voiced consonant becomes -o, but -āḥ (long ā) before a voiced consonant just loses the visarga; धर्मस्यास्य packs dharmasya + asya (a+a→ā).
#4
L: By-me pervaded, this, all, the-world, unmanifest-in-form; in-me-resting all-beings, and-not I in-them established.
I: By me, in my unmanifest form, this whole world is pervaded; all beings rest in me, but I am not established in them.
N: The chapter's first statement of the paradox worked out through verse 10: all things rest in Kṛṣṇa (mat-sthāni sarva-bhūtāni) even as he, in his unmanifest form (avyakta-mūrti), remains untouched by them (na ca aham teṣu avasthitaḥ). Sandhi: ततमिदं is tatam+idam, joined; जगदव्यक्तमूर्तिना is jagat+avyakta-mūrtinā (-t+a-→-d a-); चाहं is ca+aham (a+a→ā); तेष्ववस्थितः is teṣu+avasthitaḥ (yaṇ sandhi, u+a→va).
#5
L: And-not in-me-resting [are] the-beings — behold my lordly yoga! Sustainer-of-beings, and-not abiding-in-beings, [is] my self, the-source-of-beings'-existence.
I: And yet the beings do not really rest in me — behold this power of mine, my lordly yoga! My self sustains all beings and yet does not abide within them; it is the very source from which beings come to exist.
N: This deepens verse 4's paradox to the point of open contradiction — beings both do (v.4) and do not (v.5) rest in Kṛṣṇa — and names it explicitly as yogam aiśvaram, 'a lordly power', not to be resolved by ordinary logic. Bhūta-bhṛt, 'sustainer of beings', and bhūta-stha, 'abiding in beings' (here negated), are set against each other exactly as mat-sthāni and na avasthitaḥ were in verse 4. Sandhi: योगमैश्वरम् is yogam+aiśvaram, joined; भूतभृन्न packs bhūta-bhṛt+na (-t+n-→-nn-, assimilation); भूतस्थो is bhūta-sthaḥ, -aḥ before m- → -o; ममात्मा is mama+ātmā (a+ā→ā).
#6
L: As space-abiding, always, the-wind, everywhere-going, great, so all beings in-me-resting — thus understand.
I: Just as the wind, great and moving everywhere, always abides in space, so understand that all beings abide in me.
N: A simile resolving the paradox of verses 4-5: as the vāyu, 'wind', is wholly contained within ākāśa, 'space', yet space is not thereby confined to or exhausted by the wind, so all beings rest in Kṛṣṇa without limiting or containing him. Mat-sthāni, 'resting in me', repeats verse 4's key phrase. Sandhi: यथाकाशस्थितो packs yathā+ākāśa-sthitaḥ (ā+ā→ā, then -aḥ before n-→-o); सर्वत्रगो is sarvatra-gaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o; मत्स्थानीत्युपधारय packs mat-sthāni+iti (i+i→ī) +upadhāraya (i+u→yu).
#7
L: All-beings, O son-of-Kuntī, to-nature go, mine; at-the-dissolution-of-the-aeon, again them, at-the-beginning-of-the-aeon, I-send-forth.
I: All beings, Kaunteya, return to my own nature at the dissolution of an aeon, and I send them forth again at the beginning of the next.
N: This opens the chapter's cosmology of cyclical creation, completed at verse 8: at each kalpa-kṣaya, 'dissolution of the aeon', beings dissolve back into Kṛṣṇa's own prakṛti, 'nature' (a term left untranslated, unlike karman, per convention, though here rendered 'nature' as its ordinary sense rather than the philosophical guṇa-composed substrate — see note at verse 8), and he sends them forth again at each kalpa's beginning. Sandhi: पुनस्तानि is punaḥ+tāni (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); कल्पादौ is kalpa+ādau (a+ā→ā); विसृजाम्यहम् is visṛjāmi+aham (-i+a-→-y a-).
#8
L: Nature, my-own, relying-upon, I-send-forth again and-again this whole multitude-of-beings, powerless, by-the-compulsion of-nature.
I: Relying on my own nature, I send forth again and again this whole multitude of beings, powerless, driven by the compulsion of nature.
N: This completes verse 7's picture: prakṛti here names the impersonal, mechanical substrate of manifestation (avaśam, 'powerless', describes the beings caught in it, compelled by prakṛteḥ vaśāt, 'the force of nature'), distinct from the personal Kṛṣṇa who relies upon it (svām avaṣṭabhya, 'having taken hold of [my] own [nature]') as an instrument of his will — a distinction the poem trusts the reader to hold alongside verses 4-6's language of pervasion. Sandhi: भूतग्राममिमं packs bhūta-grāmam+imam, joined; कृत्स्नमवशं is kṛtsnam+avaśam, joined; प्रकृतेर्वशात् is prakṛteḥ+vaśāt (-eḥ+v-→-er v-).
#9
L: And-not me those actions bind, O winner-of-wealth, as-one-indifferent seated, unattached, in-those actions.
I: And those actions do not bind me, Dhanañjaya, since I remain as one seated indifferently, unattached to those actions.
N: The chapter's answer to the problem posed already in chapters 3-4 (karma-bandhana, 'the bonds of action'): Kṛṣṇa is not bound by the actions of creation and dissolution just described, because he remains udāsīna-vat āsīnaḥ, 'seated as if indifferent' — the same phrase recurs at 14.23 for the guṇa-transcending sage. Dhanaṃjaya, 'winner of wealth', an epithet of Arjuna. Sandhi: उदासीनवदासीनम् packs udāsīna-vat+āsīnam (-t+ā-→-d ā-, voicing before the vowel).
#10
L: With-me-as-overseer, nature brings-forth [the-world] with-its-moving-and-unmoving; by-this cause, O son-of-Kuntī, the-world revolves.
I: Under my supervision, nature gives birth to all that moves and does not move; by this cause the world turns and evolves.
N: This states the mechanism behind verses 7-9 directly: prakṛti acts, but only mayā adhyakṣeṇa, 'with me as overseer' — the personal Kṛṣṇa presiding over the impersonal process, so that jagat viparivartate, 'the world revolves', by hetunā anena, 'this cause' alone. Sandhi: मयाध्यक्षेण is mayā+adhyakṣeṇa (ā+a→ā); हेतुनानेन is hetunā+anena (ā+a→ā); जगद्विपरिवर्तते is jagat+viparivartate (-t+v-→-d v-).
#11
L: Despise me the-deluded, human [as] a-body having-taken-on, the-higher nature not-knowing, mine, the-great-lord-of-beings.
I: The deluded despise me for taking on a human form, not knowing my higher nature as the great lord of all beings.
N: A turn to the poem's recurring complaint (cf. 4.6, 7.13, 7.24): the mūḍhāḥ, 'deluded', mistake Kṛṣṇa's mānuṣīṃ tanum, 'human body' — assumed voluntarily, āśritam, 'taken on' — for the whole of what he is, missing his param bhāvam, 'higher nature', as bhūta-mahā-īśvaraḥ, 'the great lord of beings'. Sandhi: मूढा is mūḍhāḥ with its visarga dropped (not -o) before the voiced m- of mānuṣīm, since the stem is ā, as in verse 3's puruṣā; भावमजानन्तो packs bhāvam+ajānantaḥ (-aḥ before m-→-o); भूतमहेश्वरम् packs bhūta-mahā-īśvaram (ā+ī→e).
#12
L: Of-vain-hope, of-vain-action, of-vain-knowledge, senseless — [they], a-demonic and-asuric, deluding nature, resorting-to.
I: Vain in their hopes, vain in their deeds, vain in their knowledge, senseless, they cling to a demonic, titanic, and deluding nature.
N: This describes the mūḍhāḥ of verse 11 further, in a cascade of bahuvrīhi compounds each meaning 'whose X is vain' (mogha-āśa, mogha-karman, mogha-jñāna), culminating in the diagnosis that they have taken rākṣasīm āsurīṃ ... prakṛtiṃ mohinīm, 'a demonic, titanic, and deluding nature', as their own — the same prakṛti of verses 7-10 now specified in its lower, binding aspect. Sandhi: मोघाशा packs mogha+āśāḥ (a+ā→ā, then visarga dropped before voiced m-); मोघकर्माणो is mogha-karmāṇaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o; चैव is ca+eva (a+e→ai).
#13
L: But-the-great-souled, me, O son-of-Pṛthā, the-divine nature having-resorted-to, worship-with-minds-on-nothing-else, having-known [me as] the-origin-of-beings, imperishable.
I: But the great souls, Pārtha, who take refuge in my divine nature, worship me with undivided minds, knowing me as the origin of beings, the imperishable.
N: The contrasting portrait to verses 11-12: where the mūḍhāḥ resort to a demonic nature, the mahātmānaḥ, 'great souls', resort instead to Kṛṣṇa's daivīṃ prakṛtim, 'divine nature', worshiping ananya-manasaḥ, 'with minds on nothing else' — a phrase this chapter returns to often (verses 14, 22, 30). Sandhi: महात्मानस्तु is mahātmānaḥ+tu (-aḥ+t-→-as t-); भजन्त्यनन्यमनसो packs bhajanti (-i+a-→-y a-) + ananya-manasa�ḥ (-aḥ before j-→-o).
#14
L: Constantly praising me and-striving, of-firm-vows, and-doing-homage-to me with-devotion, ever-disciplined, they-worship.
I: Constantly glorifying me, striving with firm resolve, bowing to me in devotion, ever disciplined, they worship me.
N: This elaborates verse 13's worship in practical terms — praising (kīrtayantaḥ), striving (yatantaḥ), bowing (namasyantaḥ) — all done nitya-yuktāḥ, 'ever disciplined', the same constancy the poem has praised since 6.30's sadā-yukta. Sandhi: कीर्तयन्तो is kīrtayantaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o (a pattern now well established, occurring more than a dozen times in this chapter and not separately flagged from here on except where a new consonant is involved); यतन्तश्च and नमस्यन्तश्च both show -aḥ+c-→-aś c-.
#15
L: By-the-sacrifice-of-knowledge and-also-others, sacrificing, me worship, as-one, as-separate, in-many-ways, facing-every-direction.
I: And others, worshiping through the sacrifice of knowledge, revere me as one, as many, or in the manifold form that faces every direction.
N: A third mode of approaching Kṛṣṇa, alongside the devotional worship of verses 13-14: jñāna-yajña, 'the sacrifice of knowledge', by which some worship him ekatvena, 'as one' (i.e. as identical with the self, the non-dual reading), others pṛthaktvena, 'as separate' (a distinct personal God), and others still bahudhā viśvato-mukham, 'in many forms, facing every direction' (worship of the universal or manifold divine form, anticipating the theophany of chapter 11). Sandhi: चाप्यन्ये packs ca+api (a+a→ā) + api+anye (i+a→y a-); यजन्तो is yajantaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o.
#16
L: I [am] the-kratu, I [am] the-sacrifice, the-svadhā I, I [am] the-medicinal-herb; the-mantra I, I indeed [am] the-ghee, I [am] the-fire, I [am] the-oblation.
I: I am the sacrificial rite, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to the ancestors, I am the healing herb; I am the sacred formula, I am also the clarified butter, I am the fire, and I am what is poured into it.
N: The first of the chapter's two great catalog verses (with verse 17): Kṛṣṇa identifies himself with every element of the Vedic sacrifice — the rite itself (kratu), the sacrifice (yajña), the ancestral offering (svadhā), the healing herb used in it (auṣadha), the sacred formula spoken over it (mantra), the ghee poured (ājya), the fire it feeds (agni), and the oblation itself (huta) — collapsing the entire ritual apparatus into a single identity, so that no part of sacrifice stands outside him. Sandhi: क्रतुरहं is kratuḥ+aham (-uḥ+a-→-ur a-); स्वधाहमहमौषधम् packs svadhā+aham (ā+a→ā) + aham+aham (a+a→ā) + aham+auṣadham (a+au→au); मन्त्रोऽहमहमेवाज्यमहमग्निरहं packs mantraḥ+aham (avagraha) + eva+ājyam (a+ā→ā), with the remaining aham's simply written joined before vowels without further change.
#17
L: The-father I of-this world, the-mother, the-ordainer, the-grandfather; the-object-of-knowledge, the-purifier, the-syllable-Om, the-Ṛc and-the-Sāman, and the-Yajus indeed.
I: I am the father of this world, its mother, its sustainer, its grandfather; I am what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Ṛgveda, the Sāmaveda and the Yajurveda as well.
N: The second catalog verse continues verse 16's identification, now with the roles of kinship (father, mother, ordainer, grandfather) and then with the sacred syllable Om and the three Vedas themselves (ṛc, sāman, yajus) — echoing 7.8's 'the syllable Om in all the Vedas' but now naming each Veda by name. Ṛk-sāma is one printed token joining two separate words, ṛc (reverting to its guttural allomorph -k before s-) and sāman. Sandhi: पिताहमस्य packs pitā+aham (ā+a→ā) + aham+asya, joined; जगतो is jagataḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o; पवित्रमोंकार shows oṃkāraḥ's own visarga simply dropping before the following word's initial ṛ- (a non-a vowel), the same rule already seen for -āḥ before voiced consonants but here applying to any vowel; यजुरेव is yajuḥ+eva (-uḥ+e-→-ur e-, matching kratuḥ+aham's pattern in verse 16 but now before a vowel rather than a nasal-initial word).
#18
L: The-goal, the-supporter, the-lord, the-witness, the-abode, the-refuge, the-friend, the-origin, the-dissolution, the-station, the-treasure-house, the-imperishable seed.
I: I am the goal, the sustainer, the lord, the witness, the dwelling, the refuge, the friend; I am the source, the end, the foundation, the treasury, and the imperishable seed.
N: A third catalog, without the repeated 'I am' of verses 16-17 but continuing the same construction (each noun a further predicate nominative in apposition to an implied aham): twelve names for Kṛṣṇa as the world's beginning, end and constant support, closing on bījam avyayam, 'the imperishable seed' — the same organic image of a seed containing its own unfolding used elsewhere for prakṛti and puruṣa together. Sandhi: गतिर्भर्ता is gatiḥ+bhartā (-iḥ+bh-→-ir bh-); बीजमव्ययम् is bījam+avyayam, joined.
#19
L: I-give-heat; I withhold-and-release the-rain; immortality and-indeed death, and-being and-non-being I, O Arjuna.
I: I give forth heat; I hold back the rain and I send it out again. I am immortality and also death, and I am being and non-being too, Arjuna.
N: The catalog verses close by pairing opposites within Kṛṣṇa himself: heat and rain (a nod to his control of the sun and monsoon), amṛta and mṛtyu ('the deathless' and 'death'), and finally sat and asat, 'being' and 'non-being' — the same pair used at 13.12 and 11.37 for the ultimate reality beyond ordinary categories. The first token of the verse fuses three words: tapāmi+aham+aham. Sandhi: निगृह्णाम्युत्सृजामि is nigṛhṇāmi+utsṛjāmi (-i+u-→-y u-); मृत्युश्च is mṛtyuḥ+ca (-uḥ+c-→-uś c-); सदसच्चाहमर्जुन packs sat+asat (-t+a-→-d a-) + asat+ca (-t+c-→-c c-) + ca+aham (a+a→ā), all fused into one printed word.
#20
L: The-threefold-Veda-knowers, Soma-drinkers, purified-of-sin, having-sacrificed with-sacrifices, pray-for the-goal-of-heaven; they, having-attained that merit, enjoy Indra's-world-of-the-gods — divine, in-heaven, the-pleasures-of-the-gods.
I: Those versed in the three Vedas, who drink the soma and are purified of sin, worship me with sacrifices and pray to reach heaven; having earned that merit, they reach the heaven of Indra and there enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods.
N: The chapter's first four-line (triṣṭubh) verse turns to a pointed critique of Vedic ritualists (traividyāḥ, 'knowers of the three Vedas', somapāḥ, 'Soma-drinkers'): their worship does reach Kṛṣṇa (yajñair iṣṭvā, 'having sacrificed with sacrifices' — the object is understood to be him, cf. verse 24) and does win them heaven, but only a temporary one, as verse 21 goes on to say. The Wikisource print line breaks the compound sura-indra-lokam, 'the world of Indra of the gods', oddly across the line, splitting it into सुरेन्द्रलोक- and मश्नन्ति; the two are one continuous phrase (sura-indra-lokam + aśnanti, 'they enjoy the world of Indra') and are drafted here as two words-entries only to tile the source exactly, on the model of ch02 verse 6's jijīviṣāmaḥ/te 'vasthitāḥ split. Sandhi: सोमपाः retains its visarga unchanged (-ḥ) before the voiceless p- of pūtapāpāḥ; पूतपापा drops its visarga before the voiced य- of yajñaiḥ across the line-break, since the stem is ā; यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा is yajñaiḥ+iṣṭvā (-aiḥ+i-→-air i-); दिव्यान्दिवि packs divyān+divi, written joined with no change (-n before d-).
#21
L: They, that heaven-world, vast, having-enjoyed, when-merit [is] exhausted, the-mortal-world enter; thus the-dharma-of-the-triple-Veda having-followed, the-going-and-coming, desirers-of-desires, obtain.
I: Having enjoyed that vast world of heaven, they enter the world of mortals again once their merit is used up; thus, having followed the discipline of the triple Veda, desiring only desires, they win nothing but a coming and going.
N: This completes verse 20's critique: the heaven so won is finite — kṣīṇe puṇye, 'when the merit [that bought it] is exhausted' — and its enjoyers fall back to martya-lokam, 'the world of mortals'. Gata-āgatam, 'the going and the coming', names the resulting cycle directly, and kāma-kāmāḥ, 'desirers of desires' (a doubled-root bahuvrīhi echoing verse 9's udāsīna-vat construction), diagnoses its cause: desire for particular results rather than for Kṛṣṇa himself, the same critique leveled at Vedic ritualists since 2.42-44. Trayī-dharma, 'the dharma of the triple Veda' i.e. Vedic ritual religion, keeps dharma untranslated per convention even in this narrower, ritual sense. Sandhi: त्रयीधर्ममनुप्रपन्ना packs trayī-dharmam+anuprapannāḥ, joined, with the compound's own visarga then dropping before the voiced ग- of gatāgatam across the line-break; गतागतं is gata+āgatam (a+ā→ā); कामकामा is kāma-kāmāḥ, visarga dropped before the voiced ल- of labhante.
#22
L: Not-other, thinking-of me, who people worship-attentively — of-them, ever-devoted, the-getting-and-keeping I-carry.
I: For those who, with undivided minds, keep me in their thoughts and worship me with constant devotion, I personally look after what they need and what they already have.
N: This turns from the fate of ritualists (verses 20-21) to the security promised to Kṛṣṇa's own devotees: ananyāḥ ... cintayantaḥ, 'undistracted, thinking [only of me]' (the same ananya- pattern as verses 13, 14, 30), and yoga-kṣemam vahāmi, 'I carry the yoga-kṣema'. Here yoga does not carry its usual sense of spiritual discipline (kept untranslated elsewhere in this chapter, e.g. verses 5, 15, 28) but belongs to the fixed idiom yoga-kṣema, 'acquisition and preservation' — getting what one lacks and keeping what one has — a common Sanskrit compound for material welfare or security; it is translated here for clarity rather than left untranslated, since rendering it literally as 'yoga' would suggest the wrong sense entirely. Sandhi: अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो packs ananyāḥ+cintayantaḥ (-āḥ+c-→-āś c-) + cintayantaḥ+mām (-aḥ before m-→-o); नित्याभियुक्तानां is nitya+abhiyuktānām (a+a→ā).
#23
L: Who even, to-other-deities-devoted, sacrifice with-faith-endowed — they too me alone, O son-of-Kuntī, worship without-the-proper-rite.
I: Even those who worship other gods, if they do so with faith, are really worshiping me, though not in the correct way.
N: A generous verse often quoted on its own: even anya-devatā-bhaktāḥ, 'those devoted to other deities', when they worship śraddhayā anvitāḥ, 'endowed with faith', are in fact worshiping Kṛṣṇa himself (mām eva), though avidhi-pūrvakam, 'not according to the proper method' — since they do not recognize the true object of their devotion, a point verse 24 explains. Sandhi: येऽप्यन्यदेवताभक्ता packs ye+api (avagraha) + api+anya (i+a→y a-), with the compound's own visarga dropping before the voiced य- of yajante; तेऽपि is te+api (avagraha); यजन्त्यविधिपूर्वकम् is yajanti+avidhi-pūrvakam (-i+a-→-y a-).
#24
L: I indeed of-all-sacrifices [am] the-enjoyer and the-lord too; but not me they-truly-know, therefore-in-reality they-lapse.
I: For I am the one who enjoys and presides over every sacrifice; but people do not know me as I truly am, and so they fall away.
N: This explains verse 23's avidhi-pūrvakam: Kṛṣṇa is bhoktā ca prabhuḥ eva ca, 'both the enjoyer and the lord', of every sacrifice whatsoever, but those who worship other deities do not know this tattvena, 'in [my true] reality', and so cyavanti, 'fall away' — presumably back into the cycle of rebirth described for ritualists in verses 20-21. Sandhi: प्रभुरेव is prabhuḥ+eva (-uḥ+e-→-ur e-); मामभिजानन्ति is mām+abhijānanti, joined; तत्त्वेनातश्च्यवन्ति packs tattvena+ataḥ (ā+a→ā) + ataḥ+cyavanti (-aḥ+c-→-aś c-).
#25
L: Go the-gods-vowed to-the-gods; to-the-ancestors go the-ancestors-vowed; to-the-beings go the-beings'-sacrificers; go my-worshipers too to-me.
I: Those devoted to the gods go to the gods, those devoted to the ancestors go to the ancestors, those who sacrifice to spirits go to the spirits — but my worshipers come to me.
N: A chiastic list matching each kind of worshiper to the destination proper to their worship: deva-vratāḥ, 'those vowed to the gods', reach the gods; pitṛ-vratāḥ, the ancestors (pitṝn); bhūta-ijyāḥ, 'sacrificers to spirits', the bhūtāni themselves; but mad-yājinaḥ, 'my worshipers', reach mām, Kṛṣṇa — the same principle already stated in general terms at 7.23 (yānti deva-vratā devān) and now specified for the devotee's own case. Sandhi: देवव्रता is deva-vratāḥ, visarga dropped before voiced द-; देवान्पितॄन्यान्ति fuses three words, devān+pitṝn+yānti, written joined with no phonetic change since -n before a stop or semivowel is unaffected; भूतेज्या is bhūta+ijyāḥ (a+i→e); मद्याजिनोऽपि is mad-yājinaḥ+api (avagraha).
#26
L: A-leaf, a-flower, a-fruit, water — who to-me with-devotion offers, that, offered-with-devotion, I-accept, of-one-whose-self-is-disciplined.
I: Whoever offers me a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water with devotion, I accept that offering, made with devotion, from one of disciplined mind.
N: The famous verse on the simplicity of devotional offering: patraṃ puṣpaṃ phalaṃ toyam, 'a leaf, a flower, a fruit, water' — the humblest possible gifts — are enough, so long as they come bhaktyā, 'with devotion', from one who is prayata-ātmā, 'of disciplined, pure self'. Note that pra-yam gives both the verb 'offers' (prayacchati) in the first half and the participle 'disciplined, restrained' (prayata) in the second — the same root used for both giving and self-control. Sandhi: तदहं is tat+aham (-t+a-→-d a-); भक्त्युपहृतम् is bhakti+upahṛtam (i+u→yu); प्रयतात्मनः is prayata+ātmanaḥ (a+ā→ā).
#27
L: Whatever you-do, whatever you-eat, whatever you-offer-in-sacrifice, [whatever] you-give, whatever austerity-you-practice, O son-of-Kuntī — that do as-an-offering-to-me.
I: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice or give away, whatever austerity you perform, Kaunteya — do it as an offering to me.
N: A fivefold yat ... yat ... construction (whatever you do / eat / sacrifice / give / practice as austerity) generalizes verse 26's teaching from ritual offerings to every act of life, closing with the instruction tat kuruṣva mad-arpaṇam, 'do that as an offering to me' — the practical heart of the chapter's devotional teaching, echoing 3.9's insistence that action done as sacrifice does not bind. Sandhi: यत् shows its final -t assimilating differently before each following consonant — unchanged before the voiceless k- of karoṣi, voiced to -d before the vowel a- of aśnāsi, assimilated to -j before the j- of juhoṣi, and doubled to -t before the t- of tapasyasi; तत्कुरुष्व is tat+kuruṣva, joined, no change before k-.
#28
L: By-good-and-bad-fruits thus you-shall-be-released from-the-bonds-of-action; with-self-disciplined-by-the-yoga-of-renunciation, freed, to-me-you-shall-come.
I: In this way you will be freed from the bonds of action, whether their fruits are good or bad; with your self disciplined by the yoga of renunciation, once liberated, you will come to me.
N: This draws the practical conclusion from verse 27: acting as an offering to Kṛṣṇa releases one even from śubha-aśubha-phalaiḥ karma-bandhanaiḥ, 'the bonds of action [that bear] good and bad fruits alike' — echoing 2.50's buddhi-yukto jahāti iha ubhe sukṛta-duṣkṛte. Saṃnyāsa-yoga-yukta-ātmā, 'whose self is disciplined by the yoga of renunciation', names the resulting state, leading to mokṣa (vimuktaḥ) and finally to Kṛṣṇa himself (mām upaiṣyasi). Sandhi: शुभाशुभफलैरेवं packs śubha+aśubha (a+a→ā) + phalaiḥ+evam (-aiḥ+e-→-air e-); संन्यासयोगयुक्तात्मा ends in yukta+ātmā (a+ā→ā); विमुक्तो is vimuktaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o.
#29
L: Equal I [am] among-all-beings; not to-me [is any] hateful, not dear. Who worship, but, me with-devotion — in-me [are] they, and-them in, too, I.
I: I am the same toward all beings; none is hateful to me, and none is dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I too am in them.
N: A statement of divine impartiality (samaḥ ... sarva-bhūteṣu, 'equal among all beings') immediately qualified by an exception for devotion: those who worship bhaktyā, 'with devotion', enjoy a mutual indwelling (te mayi, mayi ca te, 'they in me, and I in them') not granted automatically to all — the same reciprocity promised at 4.11's ye yathā māṃ prapadyante. Sandhi: समोऽहं is samaḥ+aham (avagraha); द्वेष्योऽस्ति is dveṣyaḥ+asti (avagraha); चाप्यहम् packs ca+api (a+a→ā) + api+aham (i+a→y a-).
#30
L: Even if of-very-evil-conduct [one] worships me exclusively-devoted, a-saint indeed he [is] to-be-regarded — rightly he-has-resolved, for, he.
I: Even a person of very wicked conduct, if he worships me with undivided devotion, should be regarded as righteous, for he has made the right resolve.
N: One of the poem's boldest promises: even a su-durācāraḥ, 'one of very evil conduct' (su- here intensifying, not softening, the dur- 'bad'), becomes sādhuḥ, 'a saint', simply by worshiping Kṛṣṇa ananya-bhāk, 'with undivided devotion' — because the decisive thing is not his past conduct but that he has vyavasitaḥ, 'resolved', samyak, 'rightly'. Sandhi: सम्यग्व्यवसितो packs samyak+vyavasitaḥ (-k+v-→-g v-, voicing) with the whole compound's own visarga then falling before the voiced h- of hi (-aḥ before h-→-o); साधुरेव is sādhuḥ+eva (-uḥ+e-→-ur e-).
#31
L: Quickly he-becomes righteous-souled, lasting peace he-attains; O son-of-Kuntī, know-for-certain: not my devotee perishes.
I: He quickly becomes a righteous soul and attains lasting peace. Know for certain, Kaunteya, that my devotee never perishes.
N: The promise of verse 30 continues: the reformed devotee becomes dharma-ātmā, 'righteous-souled', kṣipram, 'quickly', and the teaching closes with Kṛṣṇa's flat guarantee, na me bhaktaḥ praṇaśyati, 'my devotee does not perish' — a line often quoted on its own. Sandhi: शश्वच्छान्तिं packs śaśvat+śāntim (-t+ś-→-cch-, assimilation), the first instance in this chapter of a dental stop assimilating fully to a following palatal.
#32
L: Me, for, O son-of-Pṛthā, having-taken-refuge-in, who even might-be of-sinful-origin — women, vaiśyas, and śūdras as-well — they too attain the-supreme goal.
I: For those who take refuge in me, Pārtha, even if they are of low birth — women, merchants, or laborers — they too reach the highest goal.
N: The chapter's clearest statement of its universalism: pāpa-yonayaḥ, 'those of sinful/base origin' (a phrase describing low social status by birth, not moral fault), explicitly including striyaḥ, 'women', vaiśyāḥ, 'commoners', and śūdrāḥ, 'laborers' — the classes and sex excluded from direct Vedic study — nonetheless attain parāṃ gatim, 'the supreme goal', through nothing but taking refuge in Kṛṣṇa (mām vyapāśritya), a claim verse 33 intensifies by contrast. Sandhi: वैश्यास्तथा and शूद्रास्तेऽपि both show -āḥ+t-→-ās t-; स्त्रियो is striyaḥ, -aḥ before v-→-o.
#33
L: How-much-more, then, holy brāhmaṇas, devoted, royal-sages likewise! This impermanent, joyless world having-attained, worship me.
I: How much more, then, holy brāhmaṇas and devoted royal sages! Since you have come into this impermanent, joyless world, worship me.
N: An a fortiori argument from verse 32: if even those of low birth reach the highest goal through devotion, kiṃ punar, 'how much more' would brāhmaṇas and rāja-ṛṣayaḥ, 'royal sages' (a term recalling that this very teaching is itself rāja-vidyā, 'royal knowledge', from verse 2) — the verse then turns to direct exhortation, urging Arjuna (having attained this anityam asukham lokam, 'impermanent, joyless world') to worship Kṛṣṇa now. Sandhi: पुनर्ब्राह्मणाः retains -r before the voiced br- (like punar āvartinaḥ in 8.16); राजर्षयस्तथा packs rāja+ṛṣayaḥ (a+ṛ→ar) + rājarṣayaḥ+tathā (-aḥ+t-→-as t-).
#34
L: Mind-on-me become, my-devotee, my-worshiper, to-me bow-down; to-me-alone-indeed you-shall-come, having-thus-disciplined the-self, intent-on-me-as-the-highest-goal.
I: Fix your mind on me, become my devotee, my worshiper; bow down to me. Having thus disciplined yourself and made me your highest goal, you will come to me alone.
N: The chapter's closing exhortation, restating its whole teaching as four brief imperatives — man-manāḥ, 'mind on me', mad-bhaktaḥ, 'my devotee', mad-yājī, 'my worshiper', and namas-kuru, 'bow down' — before the final promise, mām eva eṣyasi, 'you shall come to me alone', for the one who is mat-parāyaṇaḥ, 'intent on me as the highest goal'. The same four-part formula recurs verbatim at 18.65, closing the poem's final teaching as well. Sandhi: मन्मना is man-manāḥ with its visarga dropped (not -o) before the voiced भ- of bhava, since the stem is ā, as with several -āḥ forms earlier in this chapter; मद्भक्तो is mad-bhaktaḥ, -aḥ before m-→-o; मामेवैष्यसि packs mām+eva (joined) + eva+eṣyasi (a+e→ai); युक्त्वैवमात्मानं packs yuktvā+evam (ā+e→ai) + evam+ātmānam, joined.
